# Sumedhapatthanākathā (Bv 2)

**ID:** Bv 2
**Section:** Buddhavaṁsa (bv)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Sumedha’s Wish

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sumedhapatthanākathā* ("Sumedha’s Wish" or "Account of Sumedha") constitutes the second chapter of the *Buddhavaṁsa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral; Lim Hwee San 2009]. The narrative recounts that four incalculable periods and one hundred thousand aeons ago, the future Gotama Buddha was born as a brahman ascetic named Sumedha [Lim Hwee San 2009]. Encountering the past Buddha Dīpaṅkara, Sumedha undertook the task of clearing a roadway, but before finishing his section, he prostrated himself across the mud to offer his own body as a bridge for the Buddha and his retinue of arahants [Bhikkhu Nyanatusita 2013]. Sumedha then formed the great resolve or aspiration (*abhinīhāra*) to attain omniscience in order to ferry beings across the ocean of saṁsāra rather than attaining liberation alone [Bhikkhu Nyanatusita 2013; Lim Hwee San 2009]. In verse 59, the text lays out the eight conditions (*aṭṭhadhammasamodhāna*) required for a bodhisatta's vow to succeed, including being human, male, spiritually capable of attaining arahantship at that time, meeting a living Buddha, having taken up the ascetic life, and possessing high spiritual attainments [Gilks 2010]. Sumedha then investigates and resolves upon the ten perfections (*pāramī*); these are elucidated through similes, including the comparison of guarding virtue (*sīla*) to a yak protecting its tail at the cost of its life, and resolute determination (*adhiṭṭhāna*) to an unshakable mountain [Geiger 1953; Lim Hwee San 2009].

Text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus reflect the foundational role of this narrative across Theravāda biographical and exegetical literature, identifying over 1,200 Pali matches [DharmaNexus]. Extensive blocks of text are shared with the *Buddhavaṁsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Nidānakathā* of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as other biographical chapters within the *Buddhavaṁsa* itself (such as Bv 4, Bv 21, and Bv 26) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns this chapter extensively with the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032) and with Sanskrit narratives recounting the bodhisattva vow, such as the *Mahāvastu-avadāna* [DharmaNexus].
